dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Coloring » Vertex coloring
dossier_meta.statement_text: Problem The valency-variety $ w(G) $ of a graph $ G $ is the number of different degrees in $ G $ . Is the chromatic number of any graph $ G $ with at least two vertices greater than $$\ceil{ \frac{\floor{w(G)/2}}{|V(G)| - w(G)} } ~ ?$$
dossier_meta.context_text: According to Jensen and Toft [JT, p. 90], the problem is due to Melnikov and was mentioned by Vizing [V] and Zykov [Z]. According to Zykov [Z], Melnikov showed that the suggested lower bound would be best possible. A best possible upper bound on the chromatic number in terms of $ |V(G)| $ and $ w(G) $ is $ |V(G)| - \floor{ w(G) / 2 } $ as proved by Nettleton [N] and Dirac [D].
